newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch up at slow start, await data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch up at slow start, await data.

text.p: Mexican stocks were slightly ahead in cautious trade on Monday, zigzagging ahead of May inflation data expected later today, traders said.
"The market is very quiet, but looks good. So far it is locals that are buying," a floor trader said. "We are waiting for inflation data, and the Dow is helping us right now."
The leading IPC share index was up 1.13 points, or 0.03 percent, at 4,161.98. Volume was dead slow at 1.5 million shares.
On Wall Street, the Dow Jones was up 41.84 points at 7,477.62.

Banco de Mxico was expected to announce consumer inflation figures for May some time today. A Reuters survey MEX22 of Mexico City financial firms forecast the consumer price index would increase by 0.92 percent during May.

Dealers said several market players were staying on the sidelines due to a skittish foreign exchange market, where benchmark 48-hour peso contracts had opened 1.2 centavos weaker at 7.9940/7.9970 per dollar.
On the broad market, of 23 stocks traded, gainers outnumbered sliders by seven to five.
Telmex contributed most to market gains, up two centavos to 18.82 pesos. The telecom's ADRs had meanwhile gained 1/8 to 47-1/8.
Glassmaker Vitro weighed the market down most, off five centavos to 23.95 pesos.
Traders said profit-takers could enter the market later.
"The market is very apathetic, you don't even hear much shouting down here. We may see light profit-taking, which would not be all bad," another floor trader said.
